You find the Brute at the main gate at dawn, pack strapped on and shield across his back. He has been quieter than usual these past weeks, which for the Brute is saying something.
"Job's done," he says when you ask. "Came north for the pay. Stayed for..." He gestures at the wall, the gate, the people hauling lumber behind you, and leaves it at that.
He unslings the shield and props it against the gatehouse. "Guard can use it more than I can." A long pause. "Nothing wrong with a wall that holds."
You ask where he will go. He shrugs toward the south: the Frozen Pass, and past it a long walk home to the Great Grove, or to Gloomhaven, or wherever the next quiet place is. You point out he has never been good at quiet. For the first time you can remember, the Brute laughs.
He walks out through the gate without looking back. Behind you, the guards take turns trying to lift the shield.

Walking near the outpost gate, you are approached by a scrawny kid in a guard uniform, which is clearly too big for his small frame.

“Hey, you all are famous!” he says with a big smile. “I worked as a caravan guard before I got this job. Met with a big Inox guy who always talked about you. He made you seem like the nicest, most amazing people.”

His smile and excitement don’t waver. “Say, my detail is doing some work to repair the wall damage from the last attack. Would you mind helping us? It’ll be fun!”
Agree to help the presumptuous kid.

It’s hard work, but the kid’s enthusiasm is infectious. He wants to know all about your exploits and adventures, and he and his detail prove to be a great audience. By the end of the day, it hardly feels like you’ve worked at all.
Tell this kid that he must have the wrong group of adventurers.
You shake your head and avert your gaze. You claim that the kid must have you confused with a different adventuring party. He looks crushed as you walk away.

A trade caravan passes by you on the road. This event isn’t too uncommon, but what catches your eye is a familiar-looking Inox traveling with the caravan as a guard.

At the sight of you, the Brute lights up and gives you a big wave, then rushes over to greet you. He is positively joyful to see you and immediately starts to reminisce about all the exciting battles you fought together.

Slapping you on the back, he implores you to travel with the caravan for a while to give you all a chance to catch up.
Agree to travel with the Brute for a little while. So what if it’s in the wrong direction?

As you walk with the Brute and talk with him about your early adventuring days, you find a hint of sadness behind his enthusiasm. He explains how he fell on hard times after leaving the group and had to resort to jobs like this to make ends meet. The Brute seems uplifted by your conversation, but the day grows late. By the time you head back and arrive at your destination, you are incredibly tired.
Regretfully leave the Brute to his duties and continue on your way.

You explain to the Brute that you have a long day’s travel ahead of you and cannot take the time to travel in the other direction. As you make your good-byes, a shadow falls over him. He walks away forlorn.

You see smoke on the horizon and sigh, expecting the worst. Sure enough, you approach the scene to find a ransacked caravan—burned, pillaged, and destroyed by what appears to be raiders.

You find one survivor among the victims who laments that when the raiders came upon them, one of the guards, a large Inox, seemed to throw aside his weapon and simply accept his fate.

That’s when you find the body of the Brute, torn and bloody among the wreckage. Seeing him this way, the fire gone from his eyes, he appears unnaturally small.
Respectfully bury the dead and mourn their loss.

Though you didn’t take the time to talk with the Brute earlier, now you take the time to bury his corpse and say a few words about his strength of body and character. The survivor thanks you for your help, and you continue on your way once more.
Take what you can find and move on.
Near the corpse of the Brute, you find an axe, presumably the weapon he threw away. There’s really nothing else among the debris, so you wordlessly pick it up and move on.

Nobody sees the Scoundrel leave. You find out the way you were always going to find out: her bunk is stripped, the lock on the Trading Post's back door has been picked and relocked out of sheer habit, and on your table sits a small, neat pile of everything she ever lifted from you. A coin purse. A whetstone. The good knife.
There is a note under the knife, in handwriting far better than she ever let on. "Nothing personal. It never was. Thanks for the company; it was more than I came for."
The guard at the gate swears he saw nothing all night. He is probably telling the truth. She was always better than the people watching for her.
Weeks later a caravan master mentions a woman in dark leather who paid her way south and spent the whole trip teaching the drivers to cheat at cards. You find you are smiling. Somewhere out there, the Scoundrel is doing fine.

“You there! Stop!”

You turn to see a town guard walking briskly toward you.

“You are known associates of this woman, yes?” He holds up a crude sketch of the Scoundrel. “We believe she is behind a number of high-profile robberies and demand that you give us any information you have on her whereabouts and activities.”

His face softens a bit. “Look, I know you do a lot of good for the outpost, but the merchants are breathing down my neck on this one, and I could really use a lead.”
Cooperate with the guard and tell him everything you know.

The guard taps his notes with a smile on his face.\n\n“This is great,” he says. “I understand that you haven’t seen her in a while, but the information you’ve provided should still be useful. Have a nice day!”
Be as vague and unhelpful as possible, giving no useful information.

The guard scratches his head and looks down at his notes.\n\n“Well, that wasn’t very helpful,” he sighs. “But thanks for your time, I guess. Let me know if you remember anything or get any new information.”

Riding up on horses, a band of dirty, rough men quickly overtake and surround your group. They look hard and dangerous, and you immediately pull out your weapons as they approach.

Then you hear a familiar laugh.

“Well, if it isn’t my old crew.” A woman in dark leather armor leaps off her horse to come greet you. “You know what, boys? This lot gets a pass.”

She winks at you and turns around. “Plus, they’d probably kill you all if things turned ugly.”

Jumping back onto her horse, the Scoundrel looks back at you. “Well, it was nice seeing you. Just remember—you never saw me.”
Attack. Friend or not, those who prey on the weak should be brought to justice.

You see the bandits relax a little and begin to form up. That is when you strike. Some are scared off by the sudden attack, but others engage you hungrily. The Scoundrel throws a few good daggers, too, before she rides off, criticizing your poor decision-making.
The bandits seem a little disappointed as they form up and ride off in the opposite direction.

“So, I hear you stood up for me with the guards the other day. Such annoying pests, aren’t they?”

You turn around in the street to see the Scoundrel emerge from a dark alley with a smile on her face.

“I just wanted to thank you in person,” she says. “I’ve known quite a few persons who would have ratted me out for their chance at a piece of gold. It’s good to know some friendships last.”

She looks over her shoulder. “Listen, I’m leaving town for a good long while. You wanna grab a drink before I take off?”
Have a drink and reminisce about old times.

You laugh for a while and trade tales. As the sun drops below the tavern windows, the Scoundrel gets up to leave.

“Listen, I really did enjoy our time together, and, well, I just wanted to leave you with something to remember me by.”

A piece of black cloth flutters down onto the table. When you look back up, the Scoundrel is gone.
Overpower the Scoundrel and deliver her to the guards.

A look of horrid surprise flashes in the Scoundrel’s eyes as you leap forward and throw her to the ground. She doesn’t even speak as you bind her arms and take her to the guard. They thank you for your service, but their words aren’t much counter to the cold, angry stare of the Scoundrel as she’s taken away.

The Sunkeeper asks you to meet her on the wall at sunrise. She is already there when you arrive, armor polished to a mirror, watching the light come up over the ice. "The temple has sent for me," she says. "They need a keeper, and there is no one else."
She does not pretend to be sorry to go, and you respect her for it. Instead she walks the length of the wall with you, laying a gloved hand on each tower as she passes, speaking a few words under her breath. The guards on duty stand a little straighter without quite knowing why.
At the gate she presses a small sun medallion into your palm, warm from her hand. "For the dark months. It will not do much. It will do enough."
Then she turns south and walks into the sunrise, which is exactly how she would have wanted it to look.

You are haggling over the price of road rations with an irritating Valrath merchant when a messenger boy approaches you holding a note.

“Sir, I have a pressing letter from an important Valrath Sunkeeper,” the messenger says. “I was told to deliver it to you.”

You reach for it, but the messenger moves back a little. “Sir, this note has traveled a long distance to get to you. If you could, please pay a small fee to take possession of it.”

You throw the kid a few coins and grab the note. Enclosed with the note is a small medallion engraved with the image of the sun. Apparently the Sunkeeper thinks the object may help you at some point in the future. The note doesn’t say exactly how and the thing has no apparent use. You stow it away in your pack.
Refuse to pay for the note.

You laugh in indignation and push the messenger away. He opens his mouth to object, then thinks better of it and runs off. You turn back to bartering, now leveraging the proof of your extreme thriftiness against the merchant.

You see them long before they get close to you—radiant balls of light blazing against the horizon.

Sun Demons.

As they approach, you prepare for an attack, but the demons have other plans. They menace you with their glowing claws, but they would rather have information than kill you.

“Where is the one you call a Sunkeeper?” one of them hisses. “The Valrath neglects her duties, and now we must resolve matters personally.”

You press for further information, but the demons get angry. “These are not your concerns! Tell us where she is or die at our hands!”
Give them whatever information you can on the Sunkeeper’s whereabouts.

You’re not sure exactly what happened to the Sunkeeper after she left the party, but you tell the demons everything you know.\nThey seem satisfied with your response and even offer a bitter thanks as they fly off to the west.
Attack the demons. There are a lot of them, but you do not take kindly to threats.

Without even speaking, you draw your weapons and attack. The demons are caught off guard, but they bounce back with great ferocity. It is a long, brutal battle, and you continue on in your adventure greatly wounded and bloody.

You are heading through a small forest when you hear the sound of a woman screaming off to the west. You silently move closer, catching a glimpse of multiple radiant figures through the trees.

They are Sun Demons, perhaps the same ones who accosted you earlier. That suspicion is confirmed when you get closer and see they are hovering around an armored Valrath woman bound to a tree, torturing her for information.

“Don’t you see how important this is!” one of the demons says. “Give us the location of the temple!”

“Lies and tricks of a demon,” the Sunkeeper responds. “The temple is in no danger except from you.”
Leave the scene quietly and return to your own business.
Not wanting to get involved, you simply move on. Eventually the screams of the Sunkeeper fade away.
Attack the demons and free the Sunkeeper.

You charge out of the trees and attack the Sun Demons. Fueled by righteous indignation and a bit of guilt, you slay them all. The battle leaves you wounded, but the Sunkeeper happily mends your wounds once you free her.\n\n“They seemed to think the Sun Temple is under attack by Night Demons,” she says. “I have no reason to believe them, but still, would you mind helping me look into it?”

By now, the Sun Demons cut a very recognizable portrait against the horizon as they move toward you. You sincerely had hoped you were done with these creatures.

“We have urgent need of your assistance,” one of them starts. “Night Demons have infested the Sun Temple, attempting to desecrate it and send the world into eternal darkness.

“We have tried to stop them, but they are too fortified inside the temple. We regrettably need more strength.

“Please, you cannot want an absence of a sun on this plane any less than we do. It would be disastrous.”
Agree to help the Sun Demons.
You sigh and agree, warning them that this had better be the last time they ask you for a favor. They give you the location of the Sun Temple and implore you to hurry.
Attack the Sun Demons. It may be the only way to stop them from bothering you.

Without even speaking, you draw your weapons and attack. The demons are caught off guard, but they bounce back with great ferocity. It is a long, brutal battle, and you continue on in your adventure greatly wounded and bloody.

Sunkeepers have been trained to tap into long-dormant demonic powers and harness them for the purpose of righteousness. The Sunkeeper has an assortment of Healing, Buffing and Card Recovery abilities and is a capable Melee fighter in her own right. She works best in the role of a Paladin, aiding the main damage dealers in combat while keeping them alive.

Role: Melee Tank/Support Difficulty: Low Strengths: • Array of buff, heal and recovery options • Competent melee combatant • Uses Light to enhance her abilities Weaknesses: • Can struggle against groups of smaller enemies • Weaker with fewer allies • Rather self-righteous a lot of the time
On each of your turns, give an ally a card, heal an ally, grant an ally <sprite name=Shield>, or place a card in an ally's active area
Deal at least <sprite name=Damage> 20 with a single attack ability

You find the Sawbones in the Alchemist's back room, labeling jars. He has been at it for days: every salve, splint and tincture he carried, written up in his cramped hand and shelved where anyone can find it.
"Enough people know how to break things in this town," he says without looking up. "Somebody ought to know how to put them back together when I am gone." He closes the last jar, wipes his hands, and finally turns around. "The sanctuary wrote. A quiet post, inland. Warm. I said yes before I could talk myself out of it."
He leaves you his saw. Not as a weapon, he insists, though you both know how he used it. "For the lumber. Honestly."
The morning he goes, half the outpost turns out to see him off, every one of them someone he has stitched, set or sobered up. He pretends to be annoyed about it the whole way to the gate.

Looking for a little bit of variety, you head to the roughest table in the Tavern as night falls. After some wait, you are surprised to see the Sawbones sitting near the back of the room by himself. Considering this corner is about as seedy as Frosthaven gets, it is just about the last place you would expect to find him.

“I just...I don’t know what to do now,” the Sawbones confesses after you sit down. “I’d like to join the sanctuary and lead a nice, quiet life, but after adventuring with all of you, that just doesn’t seem fulfilling anymore.”

He shakes his head. “I don’t know. This life seems so boring now. What do you think?”
Tell him that joining the sanctuary is the right thing to do.
“I guess you’re right,” he shrugs. “Here’s to one last night of freedom.” He lifts his glass and gulps down the contents. You follow his lead and the rest is a blur.
Tell him to follow his dreams.

“You’re right! I’m in command of my own life, and I’m going to do what I want with it. Maybe I’ll go to the Capital and start my own business or something. Who knows?”\n\nHe lifts his glass and looks at you. “To endless possibilities! The next round’s on me.”

At first the man looks dead, with numerous open wounds and lying in a pool of blood in the dirt.\n\nBut then he coughs and whispers something unintelligible. The man looks pretty bad off, likely attacked by some wild animal, but it’s possible he could be saved.
Help the wounded man as best you can.

The man’s wounds actually look worse than they really are, and your time with the Sawbones has given you some experience in what to do. You bind the wounds to stop the bleeding and then give him something to eat. He lost a lot of blood, but after some nursing, he’s able to stand and make his way back to Frosthaven, thanking you profusely in the process.
Let the man die and take his belongings.

You riffle through the man’s pockets as he speaks his last words. They’re too soft to make out, but the tone is one of anger and disappointment. You make off with a decent amount of money and leave the corpse to rot.

You head back to your rooms for the night when you see the Sawbones sitting in front of your doorstep, looking rather dejected.

“I, uh, well, you see...” he stammers, “I followed your advice. Chased my dreams and all that, but I ended up in debt to some rather unscrupulous people. They’ve threatened to kill me if I don’t pay them off, but, uh, but I simply don’t have the money.”

He hesitates. “Seeing as how, uh, you bear some responsibility for setting me down this path, I was wondering if you’d be willing to offer some assistance in getting me out of this mess?”
Offer to pay off the Sawbones’ debt.

It’s a hefty chunk of money, but the Sawbones is incredibly grateful.

“This is wonderful! I knew I could count on you. This should be enough to put this mess behind me and finally allow me to live free.”

He hands you a potion and thanks you once again for all your help.
Get the Sawbones on a boat across the Misty Sea. New adventures surely await there.

You flatly refuse to pay off the Sawbones’ debt and convince him the only way to escape his pursuers is to board a ship bound for the eastern continent, far out of their reach. He is reluctant, but eventually agrees when you remind him what unknown adventures await in the land across the ocean. You see him off in the night and desperately hope that is the last you hear of this situation.

You are trying to enjoy a relaxing drink in the Tavern when a number of large men and Inox burst in and approach your table.

“So, you must be that little creep’s collateral,” one of the Inox says. “We’re here to collect.”

When you stare at her in silence, she tries again. “Little grey-bearded man. Wore symbols of the Great Oak. He said you lot would pay off his debt if he couldn’t.”

She pats an axe at her side. “Now, seeing as how he apparently skipped town, you can pay us, or things are gonna get ugly.”
You sigh and hand over the Sawbones’ debt, plus interest. Though it feels terrible, the thugs are satisfied and walk out the same way they came in. At least it is over now.
Refuse to pay. You won’t be strongarmed by anyone.

You laugh and wave your hand dismissively. There’s no way you will be paying such a large amount of money to these thugs. Unfortunately, the Inox is not amused.\n\n“Then your payment will be blood!” she says. “Meet us in the back alley, and we’ll see if we can’t come to terms.”

Followers of the Oak are religious healers who do their best to ward off the pestilence and death that can manifest in larger human cities. Contrary to popular belief, however, there is nothing miraculous about their healing methods, as anyone who has come to them with a gangrenous leg knows all too well. The mystique of the profession can get lost amongst the screams when the Sawbones has to hack off a limb.

Role: Melee Damage/Support Difficulty: Low Strengths: • Particularly efficient healer • Has a number of decent melee attacks • Medical Packs can also increase Ally's card counts Weaknesses: • Poor ranged attacks • Weaker in parties with fewer allies or lower max health • Doesn't have as great an understanding of medical cleanliness as most doctors
Spend, lose or refresh one or more items on each of your turns, without ever performing the top action of Reinforced Steel
Loot six or more loot tokens in a single turn

The Quartermaster spends his last week in Frosthaven doing inventory. Not his own: the outpost's. By the end of it every storeroom has a ledger, every ledger has a system, and the Craftsman has stopped arguing and started taking notes.
"A party without supplies is a funeral with extra steps," he tells you over the last of his good wine. "You lot will be fine. You have the ledgers now." He taps the stack like a man patting a dog.
He has a contract waiting in the Capital, outfitting a merchant house, and he is honest enough to admit the pay is obscene. He is also honest enough to look back at the walls for a long moment before he goes.
His pack is the last thing to leave, strapped to a sled and roped like a siege engine. The Craftsman swears the storerooms have never been so tidy, and never will be again.

“Your Quartermaster friend sent me.” You look quizzically at the Valrath standing at your door.

“I’m from the Capital, and I deal in arms and armor,” he says. “I’m looking to set up a contract with the Frosthaven guard, and our friend says that you may have some contacts with them. He suggested I meet up with you once I got here.”

The Valrath shifts his feet nervously. “So, can you help me?”
Agree to help him make contact with the guard.

You take the Valrath over to the Barracks, where you make introductions to the captain of the guard. The captain seems skeptical at first, but admits that they could use an additional supply of weapons. Terms are made, and a contract is signed.
Demand a finder’s fee for setting him up with buyers.
The Valrath looks at you with trepidation, but after some persuasion, you get him to agree.

You are approached on the road by a group of men on horseback. They don’t immediately seem menacing, but they are formidable and well organized.

One of the men, who wears plate armor and has a sword at his side, addresses you coldly. “You hail from Frosthaven, correct? What say you about the politics of the place? Are you for or against military rule in the region? Do you think those fool merchants could do a better job, like they’re doing with the rest of this doomed land?”

Looking closer, you see all the men wear the signet of a tower with an eye at its center.

The armored men seem satisfied with your response and take their hands off their weapons.\n\n“Good to find some fellow patriots,” the one in front says with a disturbing smile. “You know, we have a stronghold not far from here up in the mountains. Feel free to visit there if you ever get serious about your loyalties.”
Claim allegiance to the merchant guilds.

“Well then, today’s your unlucky day,” the man in front says. “Because we of the Vigil make it a point to execute any and all commerce sympathizers we can find in this land.”\n\nThe men grimly draw swords and advance. After a hard battle, the survivors retreat, leaving you to pick through the corpses. Among the loot you find a map.
Skilled Valrath Quartermasters are known for aiding adventuring parties in maximizing the effectiveness of their equipment. After all, what is a warrior without a good sword at his side?

Role: Melee Damage/Support Difficulty: Medium Strengths: • Many item refreshing abilities • Moderate offensive and defensive capabilities • Jack of all trades Weaknesses: • Master of none • Weaker when party lacks good equipment • Always packs too much luggage
Their personal quest complete, the mercenary leaves Frosthaven for good. Someone else will take up the fight.
